research_question_ru: Можно ли отличить сохранённую поведенческую вовлечённость при нарушении порядка событий от провалов поздней памяти? Насколько устойчивы выбранные измерения и можно ли по ним заключить, какая именно когнитивная причина вызвала наблюдаемую картину?

scientific_literature.title: Time Perception and Memory in Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer's Disease: A Preliminary Study
scientific_literature.interpretation: Unconfirmed between-group differences; do not promote null to proof of equivalence. Some within-group associations reported.
scientific_literature.data_availability: No verified individual-level dataset downloaded or run

scientific_literature.title: Multidimensional assessment of time perception along the continuum of Alzheimer's Disease and evidence of alterations in subjective cognitive decline

published_results.note: Mixed by domain and time scale; avoid universal timing deficit or direct causal model

scientific_literature.data_availability: Individual-level datasets available from corresponding author on reasonable request; not received. No participant-level reanalysis here.

scientific_literature.title: Timing deficiencies in amnestic mild cognitive impairment: Disentangling clock and memory processes
scientific_literature.interpretation: Working-memory and temporal-clock processing should be compared rather than pooled.

scientific_literature.title: Impaired retention is responsible for temporal order memory deficits in mild cognitive impairment
scientific_literature.interpretation: Temporal-order retrieval can be limited by retaining memory; critical competitor to pure time-sequencing disruption.

evidence_classes.E0: Paper's published cohort sizes/results: background only, NOT patient microdata or evidence generated by JANUS
evidence_classes.E1: Synthetic 5-trial demonstration profiles and exhaustive count-grid stress: software gate only
evidence_classes.E2: Preregistered ethically approved independent participants with documented consent and reference labels: NOT AVAILABLE
evidence_classes.E3: Independently replicated clinical / neuroscientific mechanism: NOT AVAILABLE

A_exhaustive_grid.description: Enumerate all (0..5)^4 = 1296 combinations of online engagement, immediate recognition, temporal-order accuracy and delayed recall. Test R1 classifier behavior over whole input domain.
A_exhaustive_grid.input_origin: Pure enumerated integers, no patient data
A_exhaustive_grid.output: Exact outcome tally + unknown/unsupported diagnostic claims check

B_sensitivity.description: Perturb exactly one task score by ±1 point, respecting [0,5], to measure local category changes. Because R1 has only 5 synthetic trials, cutoff fragility must be reported rather than hidden.
B_sensitivity.output: Directed neighbor comparisons, label change rate, robust combinations

C_mechanism_non_identifiability.description: Construct same observed task counts with different, mutually competing hypothetical causal accounts (e.g., sequence-specific deficit versus task strategy/sensory confounding). Identical observation yields identical class; mechanism cannot be learned without extra interventions.
C_mechanism_non_identifiability.output: Identical observable result across distinct stories → inferred mechanism NOT_IDENTIFIED

D_counterexample.description: A felt-no-time self-report with adequate engagement but low order and high delayed memory is NOT physical time travel; an equal report under low attention or memory loss is also not proof of timelessness.
D_counterexample.output: Fail-closed conclusion for two mutually different synthetic profiles

E_paper_scope.description: Preserve 2023 non-significant p=.15 as negative evidence against indiscriminate claim all patients lose basal temporal order; no unwarranted equivalence or mechanism proof.
E_paper_scope.output: Paper provenance and bounded claim ceilings with original publication links

gates.name: EXACT_ENUMERATION
gates.required: 1296 synthetic profiles and exact distribution over output classes

gates.name: ONE_FLIP_STABILITY
gates.required: Publish fragility estimate and avoid selecting only easy toy profiles

gates.name: IDENTIFIABILITY
gates.required: Same observed data under different latent stories must not yield distinct alleged causal diagnoses

gates.name: AWARENESS_NOT_MEMORY
gates.required: Observable engagement does not certify consciousness; report of temporal absence does not certify it either

gates.name: CLINICAL_CEILING
gates.required: No individual diagnosis, calibrated patient risk or Alzheimer's classification

gates.name: REPRODUCIBILITY
gates.required: Deterministic stdlib, no network, no human data, PR and main GitHub Actions

gates.name: INDEPENDENT_DATA
gates.required: No external patient-level data examined; scientific claim stays HOLD

next_steps: Seek open or properly licensed anonymized participant-level task datasets with BOTH immediate recognition, order, delayed recall and independent attention measurements; confirm access/consent/license before use.
If available, pre-register factor models and controls for aphasia, sensory impairments, medications, baseline cognitive state and task demands.
Use independent cohorts and power calculations; avoid fitting clinical thresholds to same data or assuming dementia represents subjective timelessness.
